objective: Ship a greenfield Tauri + Rust desktop app for encrypted point-to-point peer chat over HTTP, with GraphPact installed as the project lifecycle.
non_goals: No group/mesh chat or multi-peer rooms
No central relay, discovery service, or Tor integration
No mobile packaging in this change
No password-based key recovery or cloud key backup
grill: User asked for HTTP point-to-point P2P: each peer exposes a local HTTP API and dials the other peer by URL; no WebRTC.
Assumed exactly one active remote peer per session (true point-to-point).
Assumed X25519 ECDH + HKDF-SHA256 + AES-256-GCM for session encryption with local-only private keys.
Pre-mortem: most plausible failure is accepting ciphertext from a third party after handshake — mitigate by binding the session to the peer public key established at handshake.
Follow-up instruction to manage the project with GraphPact confirms contract approval for this bootstrap change; no irreversible live actions are in scope.

risk.rationale: Cryptographic identity, encrypted messaging, HTTP input parsing, and concurrent peer I/O.

acceptance.criterion: GraphPact 0.2.0 files are present and the checker reports its version.
ECDH session keys encrypt and decrypt a message successfully; tampered ciphertext is rejected.
Two in-process peers complete handshake and exchange one encrypted message over HTTP.
The Tauri Rust backend compiles with the chat commands linked.
The bootstrap GraphPact contract validates against the local checker.

execution.rationale: Greenfield walking skeleton: crypto, HTTP peer, Tauri commands, and UI share one integration path; lots are dependent.

tasks.outcome: Copy GraphPact skill, checker, and agent instructions into the repository.
Implement identity, session crypto, and HTTP peer endpoints with tests.
tasks.verification: cd src-tauri && cargo test --lib crypto && cargo test --test p2p_http

tasks.outcome: Wire Tauri commands and a minimal chat UI to the peer core.
Record GraphPact evidence, independent review, and project management docs.
